chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Abū Jamīlah and Muḥammad his brother, from their father, from Abū Jamīlah, from ʿUmar ibn Ḥanẓalah, from the Shaykh عليه السلام, who said:
If a woman becomes pure before the rising of dawn, she performs the maghrib and the latter ʿishaʾ prayers; and if she becomes pure before the sun sets, she performs the zuhr and ʿasr prayers.

The proper way of reconciling these reports is that we say: if the woman becomes pure after the sun’s decline until four qadam have passed from it, then it is obligatory upon her to make up both zuhr and ʿasr together. If she becomes pure after the passing of four qadam, then only the makeup of ʿasr is obligatory upon her, and it is recommended for her to make up zuhr if her purity continues until sunset.

Likewise, the makeup of maghrib and ʿishaʾ is obligatory upon her until midnight, and it is recommended for her to make them up until the time of dawn’s rising. In this way, there is no contradiction between the reports.

key_terms.طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ: the rising of dawn, marking the end of the night prayer period
key_terms.قَضَاءُ: makeup performance of a missed prayer
key_terms.نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ: midnight, a legal limit for obligation in this context

ai.seo_question: What prayers must a menstruating woman make up if she becomes pure before sunset or before dawn?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling for a menstruating woman who becomes pure near the end of the prayer times. It explains which prayers are obligatory for her to make up depending on when purity occurs, and it also presents a method for reconciling apparently differing hadith reports on this issue.
